A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across section and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on parity, number multiplication, GSM8K, and MATH, including appendix ablations and model completions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds noisy-parity experiments and another partial-chain-of-thought experiment.

M1.justification: The architectures, objectives, rewards, and pre-training/post-training procedures are retained. Algorithm 2 corrects an iterate label from t+1/2 to t+1, matching the update already used in v1's proof; this does not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: New Appendix C.3 extends parity coverage to corrupted demonstrations: final-token noise and recursively accumulated noise throughout the output. Multiplication, GSM8K, MATH, and the existing clean and partial-chain parity settings remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their methods. The added noise experiments reuse STaR with end-to-end or chain-of-thought rewards, REINFORCE, and GRPO; they introduce no new comparator.

E3.justification: The added experiments specify final-token noise rates of 0.1 and 0.2, all-token rates of 0.01 and 0.1, and corresponding temperature and training-budget settings. Figure 15 adds the partial-chain mixture (p_cot, p_odd)=(0.1, 0.35). Previously reported protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a substantial robustness study testing whether pre-training and RL still succeed with erroneous demonstrations, across noise mechanisms, strengths, algorithms, and sampling temperatures. Expanded C.2 also tests whether more partial-chain demonstrations permit pre-training generalization below the original p_cot=1/3 threshold.

E5.justification: The new noise figures continue the existing practice of reporting means and one standard deviation across three seeds, with medians for threshold plots. There is no documented increase in repeated runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained, while Figures 15–22 add substantial findings. Figure 15 shows approximately 100% greedy pre-training accuracy for the new partial-chain mixture. Figure 22 shows recovery to approximately 100% greedy accuracy with REINFORCE at temperature 0.5 under all-token noise of 0.1, alongside failures at higher temperature. These are additional conditions, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.2 adds a Fourier-based lemma formalizing logistic regression without the full parity feature. C.2 adds partial-chain threshold derivations, and C.3 defines noisy distributions and derives expected accuracies. Theorem 4's proof replaces the short-response calculation with input-dependent probabilities, while Theorem 5's mixture-weight derivation is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claims: RL after next-token prediction enables efficient learning from rare elaborate demonstrations, increases response length, and separates the two training paradigms. The additional evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains how final-token noise mainly changes the RL starting point, whereas accumulated noise can increase sample demands and reduce tolerance for high sampling temperatures. It qualifies the original threshold using partial-chain data and leaves a theoretical account of noisy post-training open.

D1.justification: C.3 adds explicit corruption-generation rules and noise parameters, with configurations documented in the new plots. Existing implementation, hardware, and access information remain unchanged. Reproducibility is limited by new noise-plot titles indicating 50k pre-training iterations while their captions say 20k.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior work are retained, including the claimed first theoretical separation and optimization explanation of length growth.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: new appendix subsections, expanded threshold explanations, additional organizational headings in the pre-training proof, and updated cross-references. The main narrative and overall document structure remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds eight substantive figures: the partial-chain experiment in Figure 15 and noise studies in Figures 16–22, including accuracy curves, threshold plots, and length heatmaps. Existing graphics are retained and subsequently renumbered. Some new captions are inconsistent, including Figure 21 calling its plotted all-token noise 'final' noise.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces v1's entirely deferred noisy-demonstration question with useful evidence about recovery and failure conditions, and improves the input-dependent calculation in the pre-training proof. These provide a limited net benefit. The gain is constrained by new errors: C.2 Equation (17) gives a negative stopping probability for Figure 15's mixture when x3=1, and several noise captions contradict their plot labels.
